Deuter.23.12.11-c.html:
Deuteronomy 23:12.11

Siluq is missing from last word in verse, add note 'c'.
Credit: Sefaria.org.

Every verse should end with a siluq accent. No siluq is present in this word (a meteg occurs on the initial he).

The most likely position for a siluq on this word is under the nun.

Ben Denckla: BHL has a vertical bar (equivalent to Unicode meteg) under both the he and the nun; BHL Appendix A has a vertical bar (equivalent to Unicode meteg) only under he. That is, the BHL text adds a siluq under the nun while aware it is missing in the LC text.

Deuter.24.16.11-c.html:
Deuteronomy 24:16.11

Deuteronomy 24:16.11

In the LC the shin has no shin/sin dots.

Credit: Sefaria.org.

The "Miqra according to the Masorah" shows a shin dot on the shin.

The UXLC has 46 shin consonants that lack either shin or sin dots. Forty-three of these shin consonants are the second shin in the word "יששכר", yissakhar (The 5-th son of Leah), which traditionally has no shin/sin dots. The remaining 3 shins without either shin or sin dots are Deut 24:16.1, Isa 46:4.6, and Hag 1:10.5.

This is probably a scribal error. Note that the UXLC has 58,195 shins in its normal and qere tags. Of these shins, 3, representing 0.0052% of the total qere shins, are in error in this way.

Ben Denckla

Deuter.28.27.6-q.html:
Deuteronomy 28:27.6

Remove unsupported dagesh in tet. Add note 'q'. [וּבַטְּחֹרִ֔ים]
Credit: Sefaria.org.

Example from BHL "Qere and Ketiv", p. xx, on "ketiv that cannot carry a dagesh that is due in the qere". The ketiv body text is ובעפלים; the qere in the left margin is ובטחרים. The ayin in the ketiv cannot carry a dagesh so the tet would be without a dagesh. The BHL adds a dagesh in the tet which is unsupported by the LC text. The qere/ketiv pair is a euphemism (tumors instead of hemorrhoids) that occurs in 1 Sam 5:6.10 and 1 Sam 5:12.7.

BHL has a dagesh in the tet, וּבַטְּחֹרִ֔ים. BHLA has no entry for this verse.

CVK

Note index
Deuter.5.18.2-c.html:
Deuteronomy

Deuteronomy 5:18.2

The UXLC follows the LC manuscript in placing the siluq (= Unicode meteg) before the etnachta.

The ordering of the marks on the aleph in the LC itself is incorrect.

The word occurs in the Deuteronomy Decalogue and has markings for Lower and Upper cantillation systems. With these dual markings the first (right-to-left) marking is for the Lower system, the second is for the Upper system. In the Upper system, the verse contains only two verses and the word is final.

The siluq is for the Upper system because the chanted verse ends at this word. The expected order of accents is etnachta then siluq. The correct ordering appears in the word's parallel in Ex 20:14 in the LC and UXLC.

Ben Denckla
